reason: Start with the stem-cell lineage to build the living component of bone.
expectation: The signalling environment will produce bone-lineage cells, though their exact maturity is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Mineralizing the collagen framework also seems necessary, but I want to establish the cells first.

effect: The lineage produced matrix-making osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes, establishing the living bone component.
reaction: The transition from osteoblasts to embedded osteocytes is a useful detail.
reason: Mineralize the collagen framework to build the arm bones' structural material.
expectation: The mineral will reinforce the collagen framework, producing mineralized bone material; I am unsure whether it will already count as living bone.

alternatives.reason: Blood vessels should support the bone cells, but I want to prepare the framework first.

effect: The framework is now mineralised, with collagen contributing toughness and mineral resisting compression.
reaction: The contrast between the two materials makes their roles clear.
reason: Combine the bone cells with blood vessels to prepare the living component of the bones.
expectation: The vessels will supply the bone cells, creating a vascular living component that can be incorporated into the framework.

alternatives.reason: The joint sleeve also needs lining, but I want to continue building the bone first.

effect: The bone cells are now linked to a blood supply, with nutrients reaching osteocytes through fluid-filled channels.
reaction: The distinction between the vessel and the tiny channels is helpful.
reason: Combine the vascular bone cells with the mineralised framework to assemble living arm bones.
expectation: This should produce living, vascularised arm bones; I expect the joint will still need construction.

alternatives.reason: The joint lining is also needed, but I want to finish the bone first.

effect: The mineralised framework and vascular bone cells now form living arm bones; the joint still needs assembly.
reaction: The cutaway reinforces how nutrients reach embedded bone cells.
reason: Line the fibrous sleeve with synovial membrane to prepare the joint capsule.
expectation: The membrane will line the sleeve and contribute slippery joint fluid, while leaving the cartilage surfaces uncovered.

alternatives.reason: Cartilage also needs to be added to the bone ends, but I want to prepare the capsule first.

effect: The sleeve is now lined by synovial membrane, forming a capsule whose secretions contribute to joint fluid.
reaction: The distinction between the lining and the fluid is clear.
reason: The only offered combination adds cartilage to the living bones, preparing their joint surfaces.
expectation: The cartilage will cap the bone ends at the elbow; the capsule and ligaments will still need to be brought into the construction.

effect: The elbow-facing bone surfaces now have cartilage caps that can slide against each other.
reaction: The sliding inset makes the cartilage's role easy to visualize.
reason: The only offered combination brings the prepared capsule around the cartilage-covered bones.
expectation: This should assemble a fluid-lined elbow joint; the ligaments may still need to be added.

effect: The capsule now encloses the cartilage-covered elbow, with fluid helping the surfaces glide.
reaction: The cutaway clearly connects the lining and fluid to joint movement.
reason: The only offered combination adds the ligaments needed to support the elbow.
expectation: The ligaments should stabilize the enclosed joint while allowing movement.
